database_summary: Small movie database (SQLite) containing films, genres, people (names), role and director mappings, and ratings. Core entity is movies (7997 rows). genre, director_mapping and role_mapping are many-to-many mapping tables linking movies to genres or people. names holds person attributes. ratings holds one rating row per movie. Schema appears to contain descriptive attributes and event/mapping rows; no explicit temporal history beyond date_published in movies.

accepted.name: movies_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  title,
  year,
  date_published,
  duration,
  country,
  worlwide_gross_income,
  languages,
  production_company
FROM
  movies
WHERE
  id IS NOT NULL
accepted.description: Normalized movie-level projection cleaning and exposing core movie attributes. Use this as the canonical movies relation for joins and downstream aggregations; parses numeric duration and preserves original identifiers and descriptive columns. | Use for: lists of movies with attributes; joining movies to ratings, genres, directors, or cast; filtering movies by year, country, duration, or production_company

accepted.name: ratings_by_movie
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  movie_id,
  avg_rating,
  total_votes,
  median_rating
FROM
  ratings
WHERE
  movie_id IS NOT NULL
accepted.description: One-row-per-movie rating facts. Use to join numeric rating measures to movies without duplication. | Use for: movie rating lookups; aggregating average ratings across groups; filtering movies by vote counts or rating thresholds

accepted.name: movie_genres
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  movie_id,
  genre
FROM
  genre
WHERE
  movie_id IS NOT NULL
accepted.description: One row per (movie, genre) association. Use to filter or expand movies by genre membership and to count genres per movie. | Use for: find movies in a given genre (join to movies_base); count genres per movie; group movies by genre

accepted.name: movie_directors
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.movie_id,
  dm.name_id,
  n.name,
  n.height,
  n.date_of_birth,
  n.known_for_movies
FROM
  director_mapping dm
LEFT JOIN
  names n
ON
  dm.name_id = n.id
WHERE
  dm.movie_id IS NOT NULL
accepted.description: Director mapping enriched with person attributes. One row per (movie_id, director name_id) with director name and basic attributes. Use when listing or filtering movies by director attributes. | Use for: list directors for a movie; filter movies by director name or birth year; aggregate movies per director

accepted.name: movie_cast
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  rm.movie_id,
  rm.name_id,
  rm.category,
  n.name,
  n.height,
  n.date_of_birth,
  n.known_for_movies
FROM
  role_mapping rm
LEFT JOIN
  names n
ON
  rm.name_id = n.id
WHERE
  rm.movie_id IS NOT NULL
accepted.description: Role mapping (cast) enriched with person attributes. One row per (movie_id, name_id, category) including actor name and demographics. Use for cast-level analyses and joins back to movies. | Use for: cast listings for movies; count cast members by category; filter movies by actor attributes

accepted.name: movies_with_ratings
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.title AS title,
  m.year AS year,
  m.date_published AS date_published,
  m.duration AS duration,
  m.country AS country,
  m.worlwide_gross_income AS worlwide_gross_income,
  m.languages AS languages,
  m.production_company AS production_company,
  r.avg_rating AS avg_rating,
  r.total_votes AS total_votes,
  r.median_rating AS median_rating
FROM
  movies m
LEFT JOIN
  ratings r
ON
  m.id = r.movie_id
WHERE
  m.id IS NOT NULL
accepted.description: Denormalized movie-level relation joining movies to their ratings. One row per movie with movie attributes and rating measures. Use for analytics that need both movie metadata and rating metrics without multiplicity from many-to-many bridges. | Use for: analyze rating distributions by movie attributes; filter movies by rating or vote-count thresholds; join to genre or cast without duplicating rating measures

accepted.name: genre_counts_per_movie
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  movie_id,
  COUNT(genre) AS genre_count
FROM
  genre
GROUP BY
  movie_id
accepted.description: Counts number of genre labels per movie. One row per movie providing the count of associated genres; useful for identifying multi-genre movies or filtering by genre-count. | Use for: find movies with many or few genres; join genre counts to movies to filter multi-genre films

accepted.name: movies_by_director_count
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.name_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT dm.movie_id) AS movie_count
FROM
  director_mapping dm
GROUP BY
  dm.name_id
accepted.description: Aggregates counts of movies per director (name_id). One row per director providing the number of movies they've directed; join to names to get names. Useful for director-level summaries and leaderboards. | Use for: top directors by number of movies; join director counts to names for display

accepted.name: cast_counts_per_movie
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  movie_id,
  category,
  COUNT(name_id) AS cast_count
FROM
  role_mapping
GROUP BY
  movie_id,
  category
accepted.description: Counts cast members per movie, optionally split by category. One row per movie (and category when category is present) with counts of associated cast members; useful to characterize cast sizes. | Use for: compare cast sizes across movies or categories; filter movies by having at least N cast members (use in WHERE after join)
